Shiv 4 Digitally signed by Hemant Chandersen Shiv In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Date: 2025.06.16 11:18:23 +0300 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction Criminal Appeal No.124 Of 2000 The State of Maharashtra (At the instance of Shri. S. N. Mane, Food Inspector) ... Appe (Orig. C V/s. 1. Shri. Parminder Singh K. Arora Godown Keepers Vendor of M/s. Reliable Carriers Pvt. Ltd. Anant Ganpat Pawar Cross lane No.2, Byculla (E), Mumbai- 27 2. Shri. Hidayatulla N. A. & Ors. Nominee of M/s. I.T.C. Agro Tech Ltd. 31, Sarojini Devi Road, Secunderabad-5000 03 (A.P). Dismissed as per Courts Order Dated 12/07/2016 3. M/s. I.T.C. Agro Tech Ltd., Secunderabad, 31, Sarojini Devi Road, Secunderabad- 400003 (A.P). ... Resp Ms. R. S. Tendulkar, A.P.P. for the Appellant-State. Mr. Laxman R. Kanal, Advocate, for the Respondents. Coram : Shyam C. Chanda Reserved On : 02nd May, 2025 Pronounced On : 12th June, 2025 Judgment:
texts.facts: 2.1) Record indicates that as per the Order dated 12/07/2016 the Appeal has been dismissed against Respondent No.2 for not taking necessary steps within the stipulated time to serve the said Respondent. Thereafter, no steps were taken by the Appellant to restore the Appeal against Respondent No.2. 3) The story of the prosecution is as under : 3.1) As alleged, A1 was stocking the goods, i.e., Super Refined Sunflower Oil on behalf of his company M/s.Reliable Carrier Private Limited, Anant Ganpat Pawar Cross Lane No.2, Byculla (E), Mumbai - 27. Said Oil was being manufactured by A3 (M/s. I.T.C. Agro Tech Limited) for which A2 (Mr.Hidayatulla) was nominee. H.C. SHIV 42.app124.2000.doc 3.2) That, Mr. A. N. Rana (PW No.3) was appointed as a Food Inspector for the Greater Mumbai, by the Government of Maharashtra as per the Gazette dated 20/11/1984. On 04/08/1994, around 4.00 PM, PW3 visited the premises of M/s.Reliable Carrier Private Limited. A1 was present in the said premises and working there as a Godown Keeper. PW3 disclosed his identity to A1 and inspected the premises, during which PW3 found that A1 had stocked there for sale 'I.T.C. Sundrop brand Super Refined Sunflower Oil', in the company packed plastic bottles of one liter capacity. PW3 demanded and purchased 450 gm of I.T.C. Sundrop brand Super Refined Sunflower Oil from a packed plastic bottle and paid Rs.25/- in cash to A1 and obtained a receipt. At the same time, PW3 issued Form No.VI of P.F.A. Act to the accused intimating him that the sample was purchased for chemical analysis. PW3 also issued the notice under Section 14 (A) and called upon A1 to disclose the name and address of the supplier. Thereafter PW3 stirred the Oil, divided it in three equal parts and filled each part separately in a dry, clean and empty glass bottle. Each bottle was stoppered securely and sealed. The label bearing the relevant particulars of the L.H.A. was pasted on each of the bottles. Each sample bottle was separately wrapped in appropriate brown paper and sealed. The paper slip bearing signature of the L.H.A. and AHO-I of Greater Bombay was pasted over it in a H.C. SHIV 42.app124.2000.doc proper manner and tide The State Of Maharashtra vs Shri. Parminder Singh K. Arora on 12 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122705741/ 2 with a strong twine. Thereafter each sample was signed by A1 and sealed by PW3, as required in law. Lastly, PW3 recorded a Panchanama of the aforesaid entire action. 3.3) On 05/08/1994, PW3 sent one sealed sample alongwith copy of memorandum in Form No.VII in a sealed packet to the Public Analyst, Dadar, Mumbai along with a forwarding letter. On the same day, he sent to the Public Analyst the specimen seal impression of the seal used for sealing the samples, alongwith a copy of Form No.VII, in a sealed packet. On the same day PW3 sent the remaining two samples and the copies of the Form No.VII to L.H.A. and AHO-I of Greater Bombay, alongwith a forwarding letter. PW3 also sent separate specimen seal impression to L.H.A. and AHO-I of Greater Bombay, which seal he used to seal the sample. 3.4) On 19/09/1994 PW3 received the report of the Public Analyst through the L.H.A. disclosing that the Oil sample was found adulterated as it was not in conformity with the standards vide Section 2 (ia) (m) read with Rule 5 (A).17.22 of the P.F.A. Act and the Rules thereunder. Thereafter, PW3 collected necessary documentary information and sent entire material alongwith Proforma-A to the Joint Commissioner, F.D.A. to get the consent under Section 20 of the P.F.A. Act. Subsequently, PW3 was transferred, so, he handed over the charge to P.M. Waghmare, Food Inspector from whom PW2- H.C. SHIV 42.app124.2000.doc Mr.S. N. Mane, Food Inspector received the charge of PW3. In due course, PW2 received the consent of the Joint Commissioner on 31/07/1995 and then he filed the complaint on 21/08/1995. 4) In response to the process, the accused appeared in the case. The particulars of the offence were read-over and explained to the accused by the trial Court. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5) It was the defence of the accused that A1 was only the clearing and forwarding agent. Neither A1 was stocking the goods for sale nor selling the same in his premises, therefore, he was no way concerned with the alleged offence. It was the case of A2 and A3 that PW3 was not appointed as contemplated under Section 9 of the P.F.A. Act. Therefore, the action of drawing the samples was unauthorised. There was no proper sampling, because though the packed oil bottles were available, the same were not taken as sample and sent in the same condition for the analysis. The analysis of the sample was not properly done. However, the A2 and A3 have been implicated in this case on the strength of the incorrect and fake report of analysis. 6) In support of its case the prosecution examined in all five witnesses, who are :- (1) Ravindra Chitnis (PW No.1) - the L.H.A. Clerk, who filed on record the documents at Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-10. H.C. SHIV 42.app124.2000.doc (2) S.N. Mane, Food Inspector (PW.No.2) - He received the charge from Food Inspector Mr.Waghmare and the consent order of the Joint Commissioner - F.D.A. and then filed the complaint. The State Of Maharashtra vs Shri. Parminder Singh K. Arora on 12 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122705741/ 3 (3) A.N. Rana, Food Inspector (PW.No.3) - He drew the sample, sent one part to the P.A., deposited the remaining parts with the L.H.A., complied with the formalities and sent the report to the Joint Commissioner in Proforma A. (4) C. H. Dalvi (PW.No.4) - the Public Analyst under whose supervision the sample was analysed and the report (Ex.P-6) was prepared, and (5) V. V. Akkalwar (PW.No.5) - the Assistant Chemist who analysed the sample under the supervision of PW.No.4, in the laboratory at Dadar, and also prepared the notes." 7) Ms. Tendulkar, the learned APP submitted that the accused did not dispute that A1 was present at the godown when PW3 visited and inspected there. It is also not disputed that PW3 purchased the Oil bottle and drew samples from it. She submitted that, there is sufficient evidence by the prosecution that PW3 sealed the samples in accordance with the procedure in law and thereafter, the relevant sample was analysed by PW4 And PW5. Said Analyses revealed that the subject Oil was adulterated, yet, the accused persons stored that Oil with an intent to sell the same in the open market.
texts.arguments: As such, H.C. SHIV 42.app124.2000.doc the impugned Judgment and Order is against the evidence on record and the applicable law, therefore, the same be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and the accused may be convicted and sentenced. 8) Mr. Kanal, the learned Advocate for the accused, on the other hand, submitted that the prosecution failed to prove the sanction as required by Section 20 of the Act, hence , the proceeding was vitiated. This aspect was conceded by the prosecution. He submitted that the Sunflower oil bottles of one litre each were in a sealed and packed condition, nevertheless, the Food Inspector took the samples from one such bottle instead of taking three bottles as samples. This practice is against the provisions of Rule 22-A of the Food Adulteration Rules, which provides that, where food is sold or stocked for sale or for distribution in sealed containers having identical label declaration, the contents of one or more of such containers as may be required to satisfy the quantity prescribed in Rule 22 shall be treated to be a part of the sample. He submitted that even if it is accepted that the samples were properly taken and analysed, yet, the prosecution failed to prove that the subject Oil was adulterated. As such, the acquittal of the accused persons by the trial Court is lawful and need not be upset. To support his submissions, Mr. Kanal cited the following decisions: H.C. SHIV 42.app124.2000.doc i) State of Maharashtra V/s. R.A.Chandavarkar & Others1 This serious infirmity goes to the root of the case and therefore raised the question 1 All MR (Cri.) 773 (Bombay) 2 1999 (1) FAC 18 H.C. SHIV 42.app124.2000.doc as to whether PW3 was competent to draw the Oil sample on 04/08/1994 or not.
